slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A regular polyhedron has congruent regular polygon faces with the same number meeting at each vertex. There are exactly five, the Platonic solids: tetrahedron (4 triangles), cube (6 squares), octahedron (8 triangles), dodecahedron (12 pentagons) and icosahedron (20 triangles).

Euler's formula for convex polyhedra: V − E + F = 2.

Only five exist because at least three faces must meet at each vertex with angles adding to less than 360 degrees: three, four or five triangles, three squares, or three pentagons.
